The additional usage of plastics could result in a minor increase in the solid waste disposal problem. Since the increased use of plastics is only 0.025 percent of the plastics production, the adverse impact should be minor.
The second viewpoint from which to evaluate the impact of the AFES is to assume that only those actions by the manufacturers over and above their voluntary plans for improving fuel economy are attributable to the standard. Under this assumption, for all NPA's except for recreational-type NPA's with off-road capability, the only manufacturers likely to be affected by the AFES are GM and Chrysler since they are the only manufacturers projecting fuel economy below the level of the AFES.
The impact of the AFES results from those manufacturers improving their fuel economy to the level required by the AFES from their planned MY 1979 level of 17.4 mpg, including the maximum likely effect of the MY 1979 emission standard. The resulting annual savings of gasoline for the projected Chrysler and GM (including captive imports) fleet of 750,000 vehicles, assuming a usage of 11,000 miles per year, would be between 10.5 million gallons and 33 million gallons and the 10-year, lifetime savings would be between 105 million gallons.
